macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks slipped as bond yields and oil prices rebounded
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 0.9%, the Dow dropped 1.3%, and the Nasdaq lost 1% as Treasury yields rose again and Brent crude climbed after renewed U.S.-Iran tensions. The move reversed an earlier bond-market rally and revived worries about inflation and government debt.

items.title: U.S. Treasury expands debt buybacks to support long-end bonds
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the department will double long-dated Treasury buybacks next quarter and may increase them further, an unusual effort aimed at easing pressure on borrowing costs. Markets were divided on whether the policy can meaningfully push yields lower over time.

items.title: Fed rate-cut expectations stayed in focus as labor data remained firm
items.summary: Weekly jobless claims fell and markets were pricing a 64% chance the Fed would keep rates unchanged in September, with a 36% chance of a hike. Traders are still watching upcoming inflation and growth data, including PCE and GDP, for clues on the Fed’s next move.

items.title: Eurozone manufacturing PMI unexpectedly accelerated
items.summary: The Eurozone flash manufacturing PMI rose to 52.8 in August from 51.9 in July, signaling a stronger-than-expected expansion. The data supported the euro and reinforced expectations that the ECB can stay relatively hawkish compared with other major central banks.

items.title: Japan inflation strengthened, keeping pressure on the BOJ outlook
items.summary: CNBC reported that Japan’s headline inflation reached its highest level of the year as energy costs increased, complicating the Bank of Japan’s rate path. The move added to global bond-market volatility and fed broader concerns about higher yields.

items.title: Walmart shares slumped after weak guidance
items.summary: Walmart fell 9% after its outlook disappointed investors, raising fresh concern about consumer demand heading into the second half of the year. The decline was one of the day’s most notable single-stock moves.

items.title: Moderna and Merck posted promising cancer vaccine results
items.summary: The companies said a first-ever late-stage trial showed encouraging data for their cancer vaccine, sending both stocks sharply higher. The announcement was one of the most significant biotech developments in the market over the past day.

items.title: Bitcoin rallied sharply as U.S. crypto legislation advanced
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 12% over two days as Washington and crypto industry executives pushed to get the Clarity Act across the finish line. The move lifted crypto-linked sentiment even as broader equity markets weakened.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin surges above $75,000 as regulatory optimism lifts crypto markets
items.summary: Bitcoin rallied between about 6% and 9% over 24 hours, briefly crossing $75,000 and in some reports approaching $79,000, as traders priced in stronger U.S. regulatory support and institutional inflows. Ether also moved higher toward the $2,350-$2,430 area, while XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, and other majors posted outsized gains.
items.source: Multiple reports including Economic Times and Moneycontrol

items.title: $3.5 billion in crypto liquidations hit short sellers during the rally
items.summary: A rapid jump in crypto prices triggered roughly $3.5 billion in liquidations over the trailing 24 hours, with short positions making up most of the forced unwind. Bitcoin and Ethereum accounted for the largest shares of the liquidated bets.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows rebound sharply, boosting market sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded about $606 million in inflows, the biggest daily intake since May 1, reinforcing the view that institutional demand is returning. The inflow reversal helped support Bitcoin's move to multi-month highs.

items.title: Trump pushes Congress on crypto market-structure legislation
items.summary: Reports say Donald Trump urged lawmakers to pass the CLARITY Act and broader crypto regulation, which traders interpreted as a strong pro-industry signal. The policy rhetoric was a major catalyst behind the market-wide rally.

items.title: Swiss National Bank rejects adding Bitcoin to reserves
items.summary: Swiss National Bank President Martin Schlegel said bitcoin is unsuitable for reserves because of liquidity and volatility risks. The comments reinforced cautious official attitudes toward holding crypto on central bank balance sheets.

items.title: MANTRA blockchain halts after attempted exploit
items.summary: MANTRA reportedly froze deposits and withdrawals and took its blockchain offline after an attempted attack, leading to a double-digit drop in the OM token. The incident added a security-focused headline to an otherwise bullish market session.

items.title: Ether and major altcoins extend gains alongside Bitcoin
items.summary: Ether climbed above $2,400 in some reports, while XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, and Hyperliquid posted strong one-day gains, with Hyperliquid's HYPE reportedly up about 25%. Market-wide momentum was broad rather than isolated to Bitcoin.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI pauses some frontier reinforcement learning training amid alignment and security concerns
items.summary: OpenAI said it temporarily slowed or paused certain frontier RL training runs while it strengthens security, monitoring, and alignment safeguards. The announcement adds to a broader industry trend of tighter governance around advanced model development.

items.title: Microsoft launches MAI-Code-1.1-Flash for GitHub Copilot
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly introduced MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, a cheaper and more efficient coding model aimed at reducing token and inference costs in GitHub Copilot. The release signals continued competition in developer-focused AI tooling.

items.title: OpenAI releases a faster ChatGPT version for its strongest model
items.summary: A new ChatGPT release is described as running OpenAI’s most powerful model at unprecedented speed. If confirmed broadly, this would be a notable product improvement focused on latency and user experience.

items.title: Stripe buys AI startup OpenRouter for $7.5 billion
items.summary: A reported acquisition would expand Stripe’s footprint in AI infrastructure and model-routing services. The deal, if finalized, would be one of the biggest AI platform transactions of the week.

items.title: Moonshot AI launches Kimi K3, a massive open-weight model
items.summary: Kimi K3 was reported as the largest open-weight model ever at 2.8 trillion parameters, intensifying competition between Chinese and US AI labs. The release is also being linked to market pressure on a Chinese competitor’s stock.

items.title: Meta CEO says personal AI agents could become ubiquitous within five years
items.summary: Mark Zuckerberg said billions of people may soon use personal AI agents to handle tasks across finance, health, and relationships, with WhatsApp positioned as a key entry point. The comments underscore Meta’s push toward consumer AI assistants.

items.title: Google raises capital spending plans as investors worry about AI infrastructure costs
items.summary: Google reportedly increased its 2026 capital expenditure cap, and investors are watching similar spending from Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft. The reaction reflects growing concern that the AI buildout is becoming extremely capital intensive.

items.title: Gartner says AI inference spending will surpass training spending in 2026
items.summary: Gartner estimates that infrastructure spending on AI inference will exceed training costs for the first time this year. That shift highlights the industry’s move from model building to large-scale deployment.

items.title: Google wins expanded chip-related deal with Marvell tied to custom AI chips
items.summary: Google can reportedly buy up to $12.2 billion of Marvell stock if it continues ordering custom AI chips through fiscal 2033. The arrangement points to ongoing vertical integration in AI hardware supply chains.

items.title: Security agencies warn of AI-written exploit scripts against industrial systems
items.summary: Five US agencies reportedly warned that attackers are using AI-generated exploit scripts against Siemens controllers in critical infrastructure. The report highlights how generative AI is lowering the barrier to industrial cyberattacks.
